text:
ashley: Heads-up — enterprise customer Brightlane is seeing streaming disconnects with intermittent 401s on /v1/chat/stream. They captured backend request-id rq_203b4a7e. Disconnect happens ~30s after start. Can someone help craft a minimal curl for streaming + signed-cookie auth we can give them to run?

sanjay: Sure — couple quick asks first: can you grab the request headers they sent (Authorization/Host/Cookie) and whether they're using a proxy? Also any client-side error body?

ashley: They sent a screenshot of the outgoing headers (I'll paste redacted) and said there's no error body, connection just closes. Using a corporate proxy. Cookies look like __Host-signed=eyJhbGci... (I'll redact).

sanjay: Ok. Minimal curl I usually ask customers to run (replace token/cookie/host):

```bash
curl -v -N \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  -H "Host: api.redwood.example" \
  --header "Cookie: __Host-signed=<REDACTED_COOKIE>" \
  --http2 \
  --compressed \
  --trace-ascii ./curl_trace.txt \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-1"
```

sanjay: Notes: - -N (or --no-buffer) keeps stdout streaming, --trace-ascii captures TLS/http frames/headers, --include can be added to show response headers, and --http2 helps match our client path. Ask them to attach curl_trace.txt and the exact command they ran.

matt: Also add --max-time 120 to avoid long hangs while testing, and suggest running from a machine outside the corp proxy if possible to rule out proxy termination. If they must run through proxy, capture proxy logs/tcpdump.

ashley: Good call. For SSE vs chunked delimiting, what should they look for?

sanjay: They should check for an early response headers block (HTTP/2 200) and then lines beginning with "data:" — that's the SSE stream. If the connection closes without an "event: done" or final status, note the last bytes in curl_trace.txt. If they see a sudden FIN or RST from proxy IP, that's proxy/edge termination.

matt: If the backend returned a 401, curl -i or --include will show the response headers with X-Request-Id. Ask them to compare that X-Request-Id with rq_203b4a7e. If mismatch, capture both client-side and server-side logs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: edge-gateway rolling restart started at 2026-03-10T14:05:12Z, affected pods: edge-gw-*. This overlaps the customer's reported timeframe.

ashley: Noted. I'll ask the customer to run the exact snippet and attach curl_trace.txt + output of `curl -i -N` so we can see response headers. I'll also run support-tool collect --request-id rq_203b4a7e on our side.

sanjay: When they upload traces, remind them to redact private keys and replace tokens with <REDACTED_TOKEN>. If they want, they can gzip the trace and share a link. I'll pre-check logs once we have the trace and request-id.

matt: I'll draft the message with the curl snippet + short checklist: 1) run from machine (outside corp proxy if possible) 2) include --trace-ascii ./curl_trace.txt 3) attach ./curl_trace.txt + stdout (curl_output.txt) 4) indicate whether they used a proxy and its IP 5) confirm exact time they ran it.

ashley: Perfect — sending now. I'll follow up when we have their trace. :thumbsup:
